subject: physics
topicDisplay: Theme B · Gas Laws & Kinetic Theory
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The ideal gas equation is:
questions.explain: Pressure times volume equals moles times gas constant times absolute temperature.

questions.q: Temperatures in the gas laws must be in:
questions.explain: K = degrees C + 273.

questions.q: At constant temperature, halving a gas's volume makes its pressure:
questions.explain: Boyle's law: p and V are inversely proportional at constant T.

questions.q: At constant pressure, doubling the absolute temperature makes the volume:
questions.explain: Charles's law: V proportional to T at constant p.

questions.q: At constant volume, doubling the absolute temperature makes the pressure:
questions.explain: At constant volume, pressure is proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.q: Kinetic theory explains gas pressure as due to:
options: Collisions of particles with the container walls
questions.explain: Momentum change in wall collisions produces pressure.

questions.q: The average kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to:
questions.explain: Mean translational kinetic energy is proportional to temperature in kelvin.

questions.q: An ideal gas is assumed to have particles with:
options: Negligible volume and no intermolecular forces
questions.explain: Real gases approach this at low pressure and high temperature.

questions.q: A gas at 300 K, 100 kPa is heated at constant volume to 600 K. Its pressure becomes:
questions.explain: p/T constant: doubling T doubles p.

questions.q: Real gases deviate most from ideal behaviour at:
questions.explain: Particle volume and forces become significant.

questions.q: Doubling the moles of gas at constant T and V makes the pressure:
questions.explain: Pressure is proportional to n at fixed T and V.

questions.q: At absolute zero (0 K), particle kinetic energy is:
questions.explain: An ideal gas would exert zero pressure at absolute zero.

questions.q: A gas occupies 2.0 L at 100 kPa. At 400 kPa (constant T) it occupies:
Raising temperature at fixed volume increases pressure because particles:
options: Collide with the walls more often and forcefully
questions.explain: Faster particles hit walls more frequently with greater momentum change.

questions.q: One mole of an ideal gas contains a number of particles equal to:
questions.explain: One mole always contains 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

questions.q: Equal volumes of two ideal gases at the same T and p contain:
questions.explain: Avogadro's law follows from pV = nRT.

questions.q: Rapidly compressing a gas raises its temperature because:
options: Work is done on the gas, increasing its internal energy
questions.explain: Near-adiabatic compression increases internal energy and temperature.

questions.q: A gas at 27 degrees C has an absolute temperature of:
A graph of pressure against absolute temperature at constant volume is:
options: A straight line through the origin
questions.explain: Pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.q: Increasing volume at constant n and T makes the pressure:
questions.explain: With pV constant, larger volume gives lower pressure.
